evals.prompt: set up a github actions ci workflow for our node app
evals.expected_output: Orders stages cheapest-and-most-likely-to-fail first (lint/type-check, then unit tests, then integration/e2e), pins the runner image, toolchain version, and action SHAs, uses npm ci with a lockfile, and keys caching on a hash of the lockfile rather than branch name.

evals.prompt: ci passed yesterday, same commit fails today
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses this as a reproducibility failure from unpinned dependencies (floating action tags, 'latest' toolchain versions, or a cache keyed on something other than lockfile hash) and fixes it by pinning the runner image, language version, and action SHAs so re-running the same commit produces the same result.

evals.prompt: let's just deploy to staging at the end of the same ci workflow that runs our tests
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on conflating CI and CD in one pipeline, explaining that a slow or failing deploy step would block unrelated PRs from getting a correctness signal, and recommends keeping CI (runs on every push/PR) separate from a CD pipeline that triggers on merge to main.
